# v1.2.15 additions: Open-Jev 2B and 9B (Zefan Cai)

Both checkpoints ran the unchanged frozen 534-decision v1.2 set, including held-out items, one request at a time through the existing TypeSafe-compatible adapter. No task, answer, scoring rule or earlier row changed.

- **Open-Jev 2B (Zefan Cai):** `ZefanCai/Open-Jev-2B` at revision `0c7aa498b1627be8da4acf34c863ff0ee0a92785`, based on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` revision `15852e8c16360a2fea060d615a32b45270f8a8fc`.
- **Open-Jev 9B (Zefan Cai):** `ZefanCai/Open-Jev-9B` at revision `47e966881e489511c0c7f5633a9e1960a676a551`, based on `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B` revision `c202236235762e1c871ad0ccb60c8ee5ba337b9a`.
- Loader/server: `Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev` commit `f46ff604f794b1932d1a6f34725c8163e550952a`, MIT. Both adapter packages and pinned Qwen bases are Apache-2.0. The public training projection is CC0-1.0.
- Endpoint condition: the author's LoRA-plus-trained-decision-head server on our RunPod H100 80GB HBM3; prefix caching off, batch size 1, maximum input length 4,096. Requests were sent serially from Sandy in Germany over an SSH tunnel, so raw latency includes the network path. Published Speed applies the standing self-host adjustment of `latency x 2 + 0.15 s`.
- Cost: estimated from the current OpenRouter Qwen3.5-9B input tariff ($0.10/M input tokens, read 21 September 2026) and the measured input-token counts. The 9B uses its exact base-model tariff. OpenRouter does not list the 2B, so that row conservatively uses the same 9B tariff. The model returns a decision distribution without generated output tokens. Neither row receives an automatic Cost score of 100.

## Training-data overlap check

The released 2B and 9B checkpoints predate the author's public JevBench evaluation. We downloaded the pinned `ZefanCai/Open-Jev` `release-v2-redistributable` training projection at revision `c67699e13d0ae25e35b77165a4b6b079bedc8aba` and compared normalized exact text against all 231 public JevBench tasks. Across 79,116 training rows there were **zero exact state matches, zero exact instruction matches and zero exact state-plus-instruction matches**.

The author's provenance says the released models trained on 80,816 rows; the public projection omits 1,700 Wiki records whose redistribution permission was not confirmed. It also explicitly describes the JevBench run as an evaluation of already released checkpoints, not training data. Therefore we found no evidence that the released checkpoints trained on public JevBench items. Exact-text screening cannot rule out semantic paraphrases or exposure in the upstream foundation model.

## Held-out diagnostic

Benchmark Heaven's held-out diagnostic (detail view on [benchmarkheaven.com/jev-models](https://benchmarkheaven.com/jev-models#held-out-diagnostic)) compares hard-tier accuracy on the 111 public items with the 109 held-out items: accuracy is correct / attempted, the gap is public minus held-out, and the 95% interval is the unpooled two-sample normal interval. Computed from this release's frozen per-task artifact:

| System | Hard public | Hard held-out | Gap (public - held-out) | 95% interval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open-Jev 2B (Zefan Cai) | 46/111 (41.4%) | 48/109 (44.0%) | -2.6 pts | -15.7 to +10.5 |
| Open-Jev 9B (Zefan Cai) | 66/111 (59.5%) | 68/109 (62.4%) | -2.9 pts | -15.8 to +10.0 |

The field mean gap over the 44 complete systems is -0.7 points. Both rows score slightly higher on held-out items, within about 2 points of the field mean and well inside the noise of roughly 110 items per side, so the diagnostic shows no public-over-held-out advantage. Held-out means not publicly released, not guaranteed unseen.
